verdict.root_cause: checkoutservice is the caller that noticed, not the fault. Every sampled PlaceOrder trace fails on one hop - the checkoutservice client span for ShippingService/GetQuote - with no server-side shippingservice span beneath it and durations of 0.4-2.5ms, the signature of a call rejected at connect before the callee handles it [tr_07ea98356fa4]. On the shippingservice side, the newest portion of the log stream carries no quote or ship-order handling at all, only JVM and OpenTelemetry Java agent startup lines repeating every 30-60 seconds, in a stream that earlier the same window carried a healthy Rust-style server [tr_e151438f74bf]. The change log explains the mismatch: at 14:24:15 platform-automation updated the shippingservice image reference to a demo tag whose name denotes adservice [tr_625b05302b69]. The artifact running under the shippingservice identity is the wrong one, so its gRPC port never serves GetQuote and checkout aborts in the prepare/shipping-quote phase before payment and email [tr_07ea98356fa4, tr_119f459f6067]. The 14:25:30 error re-crossing follows that update [tr_c23b2d629e51]. The earlier phase - QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR pointed at a non-existent host at 14:02:13, matching the 14:03:30 onset - was reverted at 14:13:37 and cannot explain failures still occurring at 14:29-14:30 [tr_625b05302b69].
verdict.reasoning: Traces localize the error to the shipping hop and positively clear cart/Redis, productcatalog/featureflag, currency, payment, email and checkoutservice's own compute, whose self-times are sub-millisecond [tr_07ea98356fa4]. checkoutservice has no changes of its own [tr_2d896171db16] and logs requests arriving and starting but never completing, with no internal error [tr_119f459f6067]. Fast failure with no callee span rules out a slow-dependency wait and indicates no correct listener; the Java runtime booting in a loop where a Rust server used to log corroborates a wrong artifact [tr_e151438f74bf], and the 14:24:15 adservice-tagged image reference names it [tr_625b05302b69]. It is bad_deploy rather than bad_config because the mechanism is that the running artifact is not the shipping service; the fix is restoring the correct image. The specialist dismissed the image update on timing, but that ruling targeted the 14:03:30 onset and does not survive failures persisting eleven minutes after the config revert.
open_questions: What checkoutservice error ratio did between 14:13:37 and 14:24:15 - recovery there confirms two phases; no recovery admits one sustained cause.
Both log queries were truncated, leaving 14:03-14:24 unobserved, and no gRPC status code for the failing GetQuote calls was retrieved.
Whether the late JVM lines truly belong to shippingservice (rated low confidence) and whether the automation's 4-5 hour cycle will revert the 14:24:15 image on its own.

alternatives.root_cause: The QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR variable pointing shippingservice's quote dependency at a non-existent host broke the quote path.
alternatives.why_not: It was reverted at 14:13:37, yet all sampled traces at 14:29-14:30 still fail on the same hop, so it cannot be what is failing now.

alternatives.root_cause: shippingservice is crashlooping for a resource reason (OOM or limit) and so refuses connections.
alternatives.why_not: No memory, CPU or restart metric was ever queried for shippingservice, and the repeated startups coincide exactly with a wrong-image change that already explains them.

proposal.expected_effect: Within ~5 minutes of the recreate: shipping-service logs stop the repeating JVM/OTel-agent startup lines and resume Rust-style GetQuote/ShipOrder handling with prices and tracking IDs; sampled PlaceOrder traces again show a server-side shippingservice span under the checkoutservice ShippingService/GetQuote client span with OK status; checkoutservice error ratio falls from ~0.12 toward the ~0.01 baseline and its logs resume the full order/payment/email/message-write sequence.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if error ratio stays near 0.12 and GetQuote client spans still error with no callee span after the recreate, or if the JVM startup lines persist in the shipping-service stream - the latter would mean those lines were never shippingservice (rated low confidence) and the wrong artifact was replaced. Also: the prior image value is recorded as 'None' [tr_625b05302b69]; if no concrete prior tag resolves, do not execute.
proposal.risk: If the mechanism is the address/config path rather than the image, this recreates the container with the same broken config and extends the shipping outage by the recreate window. Automation has cycled image update-and-revert every 4-5 hours, so this rollback may be overwritten by the next cycle and relief may be temporary.
proposal.blast_radius: shippingservice container only. checkoutservice (its inbound caller) sees connection resets during the recreate, propagating to frontend and loadgenerator as PlaceOrder failures - the same requests already failing. No other callee is touched.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alert on checkoutservice followed by the load generator indicates real user-facing checkout failure, not a lone warning. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the fan-out of unverified dependencies gives no clear prior cause.
